payload.summary: All five amendments address verified bugs or maintainability gaps in the tank simulation's mass-conservation logic. Source code inspection confirms each claim. The most critical are fr-4-911c8bce (loss routing creates mass from nothing) and fr-4-12ae787f (NOB growth uses wrong substrate, all nitrifier growth starved by pre-debit). I agree with the planner's positions on all five.

votes.rationale: Verified in algae_growth.rs:200-204. The .min(periphyton_capacity_g) cap silently discards excess biomass — the N/C vanishes entirely. route_algae_loss_to_dissolved_organics exists at line 282 with the correct signature (state, biomass_g, n_to_c_ratio). The proposed fix — compute excess before capping, route it via that function — is minimal, correct, and directly addresses a mass-conservation violation.

Verified in engine.rs:353-366. Four microbe biomass pools are multiplied by (1.0 - setback) with no routing of removed mass. The budget system explicitly exempts clean_filter from nitrogen validation (line 530), confirming the mass loss is intentionally invisible to the budget guard — but without documentation of whether this represents physical export (down the drain) or a modeling gap. The amendment correctly identifies that either routing to detritus/dissolved organics OR documenting explicit export with a budget entry is needed. Both options are valid; the current silent destruction is not.

Verified: neither nitrogen_budget_components (line 162) nor carbon_budget_components (line 252) in budget.rs has any doc comments. The test relies on suffix conventions (_mg_n_total, _mg_c_total, biomass_g) defined in helper functions in budget_tracking.rs. A developer adding a field like organic_matter_g or nitrogen_pool_mg would silently bypass the safety net. Adding doc comments at the declaration site documenting the naming obligation is low-effort and directly strengthens a critical safety mechanism.

Verified all three sub-bugs in nitrogen_cycle.rs. (1) Lines 226-229 debit TAN before growth computation at lines 285-323, so constrained_live_growth_g receives a depleted ammonia pool — growth collapses to zero when oxidation fully consumes TAN. (2) AOB/comammox growth at lines 287-292 and 318-323 feed from the post-debit ammonia pool. (3) NOB growth at lines 302-307 explicitly uses state.water.ammonia_total_mg_n_total as its nitrogen source, but NOB oxidizes nitrite (constrained by nitrite at line 257). NOB should use nitrite, not ammonia, for its N source. These are clear biochemical modeling errors that produce incorrect nitrifier population dynamics.

Verified in all three locations. plant_growth.rs:151-157 routes unclamped respiration_g and senescence_g after flooring biomass at 0.0. algae_growth.rs:116-125 routes unclamped suspended_respiration_g + suspended_grazing_g after the same floor. algae_growth.rs:200-209 does the same for periphyton. In each case, when losses exceed available biomass, the floor prevents biomass from going negative but the full unclamped loss is still routed to dissolved organics/detritus — creating nitrogen and carbon from nothing. The fix (clamp routed loss to actual biomass removed: before - after) is correct and necessary.
